about: Statement shapes that a named downstream consumer of emulator-spark-agent actually sends, each cited to the consumer file it comes from, with the answer the agent owes it. `expect.match` means delta_ops.match() must claim the statement and route it to that handler. `expect.remember` means the statement is the engine's to execute, but the agent must record where the table lives, because a later OPTIMIZE / MERGE / DESCRIBE of that name has no other way to find it. `given` is the schema registry the statement arrives with (schema -> location); CTAS interception is conditional on it. `sql` is a string, or a list of lines joined with newlines. python/tests/test_agent_consumer_contract.py proves recognition for every case; a case listing e2e/agent-contract/run.py in executed_by is also run against the built agent image before it is published.

cases.source: e2e/delta/run.py — Warehouse SQL, the shape `databricks-sdk` sends
cases.why: A column list between the table name and USING. The agent failed to match this shape in four releases (0.25.0 through 0.26.0): the location went unrecorded, and the MERGE that follows fell through to resolve()'s DESCRIBE DETAIL and died in Sail's parser with `found DETAIL at 9:15`.
cases.sql: CREATE TABLE events (id INT, name STRING) USING delta LOCATION '/data/e2e/events'

cases.source: e2e/delta/run.py — upsert against the table created above
cases.why: MERGE against a named target. It can only resolve through the location recorded from the CREATE before it; this is the statement that regressed in 0.25.0.
cases.sql: MERGE INTO events AS t USING (SELECT * FROM VALUES (3, 'carol-upd'), (4, 'dave') AS s(id, name)) AS s ON t.id = s.id WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET t.name = s.name WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *

cases.source: internal/sqlshim — managed CREATE, rewritten to carry a LOCATION
cases.why: A managed CREATE that databricks-emulator rewrites to carry a LOCATION. The location has to be findable by the full three-part name the consumer uses afterwards.
cases.sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS main.default.t (id BIGINT) USING delta LOCATION '/data/__unitystorage/t'

cases.source: dbt-fabricspark with +location_root — the shape that has always worked
cases.why: The shape that has always worked. It stays as the baseline the other CREATE rows vary from, so a regression in the common path fails here first.
cases.sql: CREATE TABLE silver.orders USING delta LOCATION 'abfss://lake/Tables/orders'

cases.why: CTAS interception is conditional on the schema registry: a schema nobody gave a location for belongs in the engine's own warehouse. This case gives gold a location, so the agent must claim the statement.
cases.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE gold.fct AS SELECT 1 AS n

cases.why: OPTIMIZE addressed by path. Sail has no grammar for OPTIMIZE, so the agent must claim it and run it through delta-rs.
VACUUM by name with a retention clause. Sail has no grammar for VACUUM either, so an unclaimed statement reaches a parser that rejects it.

cases.source: Warehouse SQL — a decimal column, the case a naive `\([^)]*\)` loses
cases.why: Column types carrying their own parentheses. The column list has to be matched paren-aware, or DECIMAL(10,2) truncates it and the LOCATION is lost exactly as in the column-list case, without a symptom until much later.
cases.sql: CREATE TABLE priced (id INT, amount DECIMAL(10,2)) USING delta LOCATION '/data/priced'

cases.source: dbt-fabricspark table materialization — contoso-airflow-data-product dbt/silver/models/silver_product_hierarchy.sql, via logs/dbt.log
cases.why: A dbt model file opens with a comment, so the statement the adapter sends carries one between AS and SELECT. Copied verbatim from a dbt-fabricspark debug log, whitespace, backquoted relation and all, because every hand-written probe of this shape passed and only the adapter's own output failed. A tidied version would prove nothing.
sql: -- Deliberately thin: this vendor is the group data office's publisher.

cases.source: dbt-fabricspark — contoso-airflow-data-product dbt/silver/models/silver_customers.sql, the canonical `with … select`
cases.why: A CTE, which is how dbt's own documentation writes models and how most projects follow it. Requiring SELECT claimed the minority of a real silver layer: measured on one project, the three models opening with SELECT landed in OneLake with a _delta_log and the five opening with WITH left bare parquet at the same paths, unreadable as a table and reported as success by both halves.
sql: -- THE DUPLICATES ARE DELIBERATE. The POS vendor ships a 2% ratio.
select *, row_number() over (partition by customer_id order by updated_at desc) as rn

cases.source: dbt-fabricspark — a model whose header is a block comment (and the query_comment adapters prepend)
cases.why: The same miss through the other comment syntax. dbt's own query_comment is a block comment, and a fix that handles only `--` leaves this open.

Spark allows clauses between USING and LOCATION, and dbt emits partitioning this way. Writing the shapes down found this one silently unrecorded too; the LOCATION arriving after PARTITIONED BY must still be recorded.
cases.sql: CREATE TABLE silver.evt (id INT, d DATE) USING delta PARTITIONED BY (d) LOCATION 'abfss://lake/Tables/evt'
